title: Pinegrove enterprise alliances scratchpad
notes:
Quick context: Pinegrove is a mid-sized retail analytics platform (offers shopper insights + checkout UX widgets). Heard about them via intro from Nick R. at Channel Partners. They mentioned interest in an on-prem private deploy for data residency and also want predictable cost for heavy embedding usage (search + personalization).

Account snapshot (what we know):
- HQ: Boston, 600 employees, engineering org ~80.
- Primary product: real-time personalization engine + analytics dashboard for retail chains.
- Current infra: mostly AWS, some proprietary on-prem connectors for POS.
- Pain: rising token costs for embedding+ranking jobs, variance in latency during Black Friday simulations, and strict PCI-adjacent compliance requirements.

Key stakeholders (hypothesized):
- Head of Platform: Tara Kim — cares about infra cost and scaling predictability.
- Lead ML / Recs: Samir Patel — cares about embedding quality, latency, model drift detection.
- Security/Compliance: Jordan Rivers — will require KMS, VPC, audit logs.
- Product (buyer persona): Head of Product Ops / Growth — ROI on personalization metrics.

Value props to test in outreach: concise bullets we can use in email/intro call
- Reduce per-query unit cost with batching + KV prefix caching — real savings for repeated personalization queries.
- Dedicated pools for predictable throughput during peak events (Black Friday) with SLA and burst cap.
- Private deployment option: VPC + KMS + audit logs for PCI-adjacent workloads.
- Fast dev experience: same API across hosted/dedicated/private — easier to prototype, then flip to dedicated for scale.
- Quality safety: rollouts + canarying so model changes don't regress CTR/engagement.

Potential objections + short rebuttals (notes to self):
- "We already have embeddings on x provider, switching is risky." -> Ask about pain: cost spikes? cold-start latencies? Offer migration POC with dual-run for 2 weeks and compare unit costs + recall metrics.
- "On-prem is expensive / slow to set up." -> Emphasize Redwood Private quickstart for VPC and partner-managed option; offer timeline (45-60 days typical for mid-enterprise). Suggest initial Dedicated pilot to validate both cost/latency then plan Private.
- "We need deterministic SLAs for Black Friday." -> Dedicated capacity with reserved pools + canary fallback to hosted variants; propose runbook for failover and capacity buffer.
- "Security sign-off will take months." -> Provide security pack: architecture diagram, KMS/HSM details, SOC2+audit artifacts, and a named solutions engineer to expedite.

Draft outbound cadences (working):
1) Short email intro referencing Nick + 2-sentence pain hook + ask for 20m intro.
2) If no reply 5 days, short case-study of similar retail client (anonymized metrics: 30% cost saving embeddings + 40% latency drop).
3) If still no reply, reply with calendar link + one-pager on Dedicated vs Private decision checklist.

Draft cold email (subject ideas + body snippets):
- Subject: "Reduce peak personalization costs for Pinegrove"
- Opening: "Tara — quick note from Maya at Redwood. Nick R. suggested I reach out — we work with retail platforms to cut embedding spend and stabilize latency during peak traffic."
- 2-line value: "In a short pilot we help teams move to a dedicated serving profile + KV caching that often lowers per-query cost by 20–40% while keeping p95 latency under X ms. We also support VPC/private deployments if you need data residency."
- CTA: "Would you be open to 20 minutes next week to see if this might help for Black Friday planning?"

Meeting prep notes (if we get 20m):
- Goal: surface current embedding volumes, black friday traffic patterns, current provider and costs, SLOs (p50/p95), security blockers.
- Slides to bring: 1) Redwood quick blurb, 2) Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private table (cost/latency/lead time), 3) example timeline for 30-day pilot, 4) security artifact list.
- Data ask: current monthly embedding calls, average tokens, peak qps, SLA targets, any compliance constraints.

POC proposal sketch (very rough):
- 30-day dual-run pilot: route a subset of personalization queries to Redwood Dedicated pool for a single region.
- Metrics: cost per 1k embeddings, recall@k on identical test-set, p50/p95 latency, error rate.
- Success criteria: >=20% cost improvement or p95 improvement of >=30% without quality regression.
- Deliverables: config for batching + caching, dashboard access, weekly check-ins.

Pricing / commercial thinking (notes):
- For pilots, we can offer a capped pilot price or usage credits. Proposed approach: 
  - Stage 1: 30-day pilot on Dedicated (small pool) with capped $X credit. 
  - Stage 2: if successful, move to reserved commit for peak windows + optional Private deployment onboarding fee.
- Internal ask: talk to pricing to see current pilot credit thresholds for mid-market enterprises ~ $15k–50k.

Open questions to resolve (for next sync w/ Liam + Priya):
- Does Pinegrove have any existing vendor lock clauses with current embedding provider? (Jira ask: PG-1123)
- Who is the canonical security reviewer (email/contact)?
- Exact Black Friday traffic projections and dates; priority window they care about.
- Any preferences on model family (open LLMs vs partners)? Samir may have strong preference.

Action items (next 7 days):
- Draft initial outreach email and share w/ Liam for review (Maya).
- Ask Solutions Eng to prepare a 1-page Private deploy architecture and SOC2 packet (Priya).
- Pull anonymized retail case study numbers from internal library and redact (Liam).
- Create quick internal cost estimate for the 30-day pilot (include batching benefits).

Notes-to-self: keep tone consultative not pushy. Use specific numbers early to get attention (e.g., projected % cost savings or p95 latency). If security asks for Private, don't jump straight to multi-month on-prem — propose Dedicated first as low-friction validation.

Random brainstorm / subject lines bank (short):
- "Black Friday resilience for Pinegrove personalization"
- "Pilot: cut embedding cost for checkout recs"
- "VPC+KMS option for PCI-adjacent ML workloads"
